title: Integration splits over the open–closed components
statement:
Fix the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$, and let $T$ be a
separated finite-type scheme over $s$ which is a finite disjoint union

$$
T=\coprod_{\beta\in B}\beta
$$

of open-and-closed subschemes $j_\beta:\beta\hookrightarrow T$, each
proper over $s$. Then $T$ is proper over $s$. For
$\tau:A_T\to\omega_{T,A}$ and $\beta\in B$ define the *restriction*

$$
\tau|_\beta:
A_\beta\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lj_\beta^*A_T
\xrightarrow{Lj_\beta^*\tau}Lj_\beta^*\omega_{T,A}
\cong Rj_\beta^!\omega_{T,A}\cong\omega_{\beta,A},
$$

using the equality $Rj_\beta^!\cong Lj_\beta^*$ for the open immersion
$j_\beta$ ([prop-functor-package], item (6), relative dimension $0$)
and the identification of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]
(this restriction makes sense without any properness). Then

$$
\int_T\tau=\sum_{\beta\in B}\int_\beta(\tau|_\beta),
$$

where $\int_T,\int_\beta$ are the integrations of
[def-trf-integration] and $\omega_{T,A}$ is the
dualizing complex of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex]; for $B=\emptyset$ both sides are $0$.
In particular, if $c$ is an admissible correspondence whose fixed
scheme $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] has
finitely many open-and-closed components $\beta\in\pi_0(F)$, each
proper over $s$, then $F$ is proper and
$\int_F\tau=\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}\int_\beta(\tau|_\beta)$, the
restrictions being those of [def-trf-local-term].

proof.text: Properness, directly from the definition [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The structure map $a_T$ is separated and of finite type by hypothesis. After any base change $s'\to s$, the given disjoint-union presentation gives $T_{s'}=\coprod_\beta\beta_{s'}$. For closed $Z\subseteq T_{s'}$, its image is $\bigcup_{\beta\in B}a_{\beta,s'}(Z\cap\beta_{s'})$. Each intersection is closed in $\beta_{s'}$ and its image is closed because $a_\beta$ is universally closed. This is a finite union, hence closed. Thus $a_T$ is universally closed and proper. Every $j_\beta$ is a closed immersion as well as an open immersion, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a).

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: properness after any base change

proof.text: Fix the canonical clopen adjunctions. Write $P_\beta=Lj_\beta^*$ and $J_\beta=Rj_{\beta*}=Rj_{\beta!}$, using proper coincidence and the open, dimension-zero purity clause of [prop-functor-package]. The open adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ and its invertible unit are [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Its closed-adjunction clause, applied with the closed immersion $i=j_\beta$ and its open complement, supplies $P_\beta\dashv J_\beta$. Thus on these clopen pieces we have $P_\beta\dashv J_\beta\dashv P_\beta$. Denote the ordinary unit by $s_{\beta,L}:L\to J_\beta P_\beta L$ and the exceptional counit, under open purity, by $r_{\beta,L}:J_\beta P_\beta L\to L$. The open counit is the one induced termwise from the sheaf extension-by-zero counit, as specified in [def-weil-open-closed-recollement]; the normalized dimension-zero trace of [prop-functor-package] is this counit. In particular the ordinary counit $P_\beta J_\beta\to\mathrm{id}$ and the open unit $\mathrm{id}\to P_\beta J_\beta$ are inverse: on sheaves restricted to $\beta$ both are the identity, and the same identity holds termwise and descends to the derived category. By [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], $P_\beta\omega_{T,A}=Rj_\beta^!\omega_{T,A}\cong\omega_{\beta,A}$. Consequently $P_\beta\tau$ under these comparisons is precisely the restriction in the statement. All objects used here are in the finite-coefficient constructible finite-Tor domains: this includes $A_T$ and $Ra_T^!A_s$ by the preservation clauses of [prop-functor-package].

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: clopen operations and the specified units and counits

proof.text: For any $L$ in the stated domain form the finite biproduct $Q_L=\bigoplus_{\beta\in B}J_\beta P_\beta L$, the row $R_L:Q_L\to L$ with entries $r_{\beta,L}$, and the column $S_L:L\to Q_L$ with entries $s_{\beta,L}$. For $\gamma\ne\beta$, proper base change [prop-functor-package], applied to $j_\gamma$ and $j_\beta$, gives $P_\gamma J_\beta=0$: their fibre product is empty, whose module-sheaf category is zero since the empty covering forces its only value to be zero. For $\gamma=\beta$ the same fibre product is $\beta$, and $P_\beta J_\beta\cong\mathrm{id}$. The restriction $P_\gamma R_L$ is therefore $P_\gamma r_{\gamma,L}$, an isomorphism by the triangle identity and the invertible open unit of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. The finite clopen covering detects derived isomorphisms by [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative](1), so $R_L$ is an isomorphism. This uses covering-family locality, with no claim about arbitrary geometric stalks.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: base change and local detection of R_L

proof.text: Identify the inverse by adjunction, rather than testing equality of arbitrary derived morphisms locally. The $(\gamma,\beta)$ matrix entry of $S_LR_L$ is $s_{\gamma,L}r_{\beta,L}$. Under $P_\gamma\dashv J_\gamma$ it corresponds to a map $P_\gamma J_\beta P_\beta L\to P_\gamma L$. Off the diagonal its source is zero by Step 3. On the diagonal the adjunct is $c_{\gamma,P_\gamma L}\,P_\gamma(s_{\gamma,L})\,P_\gamma(r_{\gamma,L})=P_\gamma(r_{\gamma,L})$, where $c$ is the ordinary counit; the equality is the ordinary triangle identity. The open triangle identity identifies this last map with the inverse of the open unit, which by Step 2 is $c_{\gamma,P_\gamma L}$, the ordinary adjunct of the identity of $J_\gamma P_\gamma L$. Thus every matrix entry is the corresponding entry of the identity. Hence $S_LR_L=1$, and since $R_L$ is invertible, $S_L=R_L^{-1}$ and $R_LS_L=1$. The adjunctions and their invertible open unit are those of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions].

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: the ordinary-adjoint matrix calculation

proof.text:
Apply this to $L=A_T,\omega_{T,A}$. Naturality of the counits gives $R_{\omega_T}(\bigoplus_\beta J_\beta P_\beta\tau)=\tau R_{A_T}$. Multiplying by $S_{A_T}$ and using Step 4 yields the equality of global morphisms
$$\tau=R_{\omega_T}(\bigoplus_\beta J_\beta(\tau|_\beta))S_{A_T}=\sum_{\beta\in B}r_{\beta,\omega_T}\,J_\beta(\tau|_\beta)\,s_{\beta,A_T}=\sum_{\beta\in B}(j_\beta)_*(\tau|_\beta).$$
The last equality is the displayed definition of Borel–Moore pushforward [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]: its proper comparison and inverse dualizing-composition map are exactly those used in $r_{\beta,\omega_T}$ and in $\tau|_\beta$. In particular no equality of derived morphisms is inferred merely from equality after restriction.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: naturality and the finite biproduct identity

proof.text:
Verify integration of each proper pushforward. Let $h:V\to W$ be proper between proper schemes in the setting, put $a=a_W$ and $b=ah$, and let $\gamma:A_V\to\omega_V$. Use the canonical direct-image composition comparisons and dualizing comparison [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]. Composition coherence [fix-prop-coherence] and the formula for a composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] give, in these coordinates,
$$\eta_b=Ra_*\eta_h\circ\eta_a,\qquad \varepsilon_b=\varepsilon_a\circ Ra_!\varepsilon_h.$$
Here the second formula includes $Rb^!\cong Rh^!Ra^!$; the proper comparisons identify $*$ with $!$ compatibly with composition by [prop-functor-package]. In the formula for $\int_W h_*\gamma$, substitute the composite defining $h_*\gamma$ [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]. Its middle portion is $Ra_*\varepsilon_h\circ Ra_*Rh_*\gamma\circ Ra_*\eta_h$. The two displayed composition formulas then give
$$\int_W h_*\gamma=\varepsilon_a\,Ra_*\varepsilon_h\,Ra_*Rh_*\gamma\,Ra_*\eta_h\,\eta_a=\varepsilon_b\,Rb_*\gamma\,\eta_b=\int_V\gamma,$$
where integrations mean the further $R\Gamma(s,-)$ and scalar identification in [def-trf-integration]. The inverse dualizing-composition arrows in the definition of pushforward cancel the dualizing-composition arrows in the composite counit. Naturality allows $Rh_*\gamma$ between them. This proves the needed equality of the specified maps, not merely of their isomorphism classes.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: units and counits of a composite and integration of proper pushforward

proof.text:
For nonempty $B$, apply the $A$-linearity of integration [lem-trf-integration-linear] to the finite sum in Step 5, and Step 6 to each proper $j_\beta$ (Step 1). The result is
$$\int_T\tau=\sum_\beta\int_T(j_\beta)_*(\tau|_\beta)=\sum_\beta\int_\beta(\tau|_\beta).$$
For $B=\emptyset$, $T=\emptyset$ and every module sheaf, complex, and Borel–Moore section on $T$ is zero: the empty covering gives the zero module on its sole object. Thus the middle derived-direct-image map in the definition [def-trf-integration] factors through zero and its scalar value is zero, equal to the empty sum. This also verifies the zero-section case and allows any empty pieces among a nonempty family.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: integrate the finite sum and handle empty support

proof.text: Finally take $T=F$ and $B=\pi_0(F)$. The disjoint-union clause of [def-trf-fixed-scheme] gives $F=\coprod_{\beta\in B}\beta$. Here is an explicit check of the geometric hypotheses, using only the assumed properness of these pieces. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] every $\beta$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. Choose a finite affine cover of each $\beta$ by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras. Their union is a finite affine cover of $F$, so $F\to s$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The products $\beta\times_s\gamma$ form a finite clopen partition of $F\times_sF$. On an off-diagonal block the inverse image of $\Delta_F$ is empty; on a diagonal block its map is $\Delta_\beta$, a closed immersion. Consequently $\Delta_F$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset (the finite union of the closed diagonal images), and its structure-sheaf map is surjective, as can be checked on these open blocks. It is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $F$ is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. This also works for $B=\emptyset$. All hypotheses of the preceding argument now hold, giving properness and the sum formula for $F$. The restricted-section formula of [def-trf-local-term] is exactly $A_\beta\cong Lj_\beta^*A_F\to Lj_\beta^*\omega_{F,A}\cong\omega_{\beta,A}$, with the same open-purity and dualizing-composition comparisons. Thus the restrictions in this specialization are precisely those in the last clause of the statement.

Step 2: on one clopen j_beta, the recollement adjunctions give P -| J -| P; clause 6 at relative dimension 0 identifies the exceptional counit with the extension-by-zero counit; clause 3 gives Rj_! = Rj_*. Step 3: proper base change (clause 4) gives P_gamma J_beta = 0 for gamma != beta; the triangle identity with the invertible open unit makes P_gamma r_gamma invertible; only clause (1) of lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative, covering-family locality, is used. Step 5: the summands match def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward arrow by arrow, and the inverse purity/dualizing comparison cancels. Step 7: linearity, and B empty gives 0. Step 8: F is finite type and separated, checked on the finite clopen blocks of F x_s F, and the restriction is the one of def-trf-local-term.
